Subject: Reserved GPU blueprint & staged activation — Orbitus Health

Hi Liam —

Following our call this morning, attached is a focused proposal for Orbitus Health's dedicated reservation. High level first: we designed three alternative reservation profiles so you can balance cost predictability with runway for burst and experimentation. The attached PDF and activation_timetable.csv include line-by-line pricing and forecast assumptions; below are the core options and activation mechanics.

Plan A — Balanced (recommended for product teams moving to 24/7 inference):
- Minimum committed baseline: 48 A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved).
- Warm standby / burst pool: ability to burst to 160 GPUs region-wide for up to 8 hours/day with usage-based pricing above baseline.
- Ramp schedule (standard): onboard 25% of baseline at contract start, 50% baseline enabled by month 3, full baseline by month 6. Burst capacity available from day 1.

Plan B — Lean start (proof-of-concept / cost-conscious):
- Baseline: 24 GPUs. Burst to 80 GPUs.
- Ramp: 50% baseline at launch, 100% baseline by month 4.

Plan C — Performance-first (recommended for large batch/throughput workloads):
- Baseline: 96 GPUs. Burst to 240 GPUs.
- Ramp: 35% baseline at start, 70% by month 2, 100% by month 5.

Activation & operational notes (important):
- Warm-up/preheat window: we recommend a 72–120 hour prewarm window per activation tranche to prime KV caches and reduce tail latency.
- Decommit flexibility: month+3 rolling decommit window after minimum term with 60 days notice on uplifts/decommits.
- Latency/availability SLOs: 99.9% platform availability for committed baseline; burst beyond baseline is best-effort and billed as usage.
- Integration window: 4-week integration window for networking, IAM, and KMS key rotation prior to first activation tranche.

Commercials snapshot (covered in PDF):
- Baseline unit rate (per GPU-month) varies by plan; volume discounts kick in at >=72 GPU baseline.
- Warm standby credits: we include 10% monthly credit vs usage for measured warm standby utilization as an offset for prewarm costs (subject to activation profile).

Next steps — can you confirm which plan direction you prefer (A / B / C) and whether Procurement needs any special terms (e.g., net-60 vs net-45, SOC2 evidence)? I’ll loop in Legal and CS for final SOW adjustments once you pick a direction.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0173

Irene — thanks for the thorough read. A couple quick clarifying items from our side before we pick Plan A/B/C: 

1) Minimum baseline: for regulatory reasons we need a formal statement in the SOW that baseline capacity will maintain dedicated isolation and that preemption is not permitted on the committed baseline. Can you add that language?

2) Warm standby credits: 10% credit sounds fair — can you confirm how credits apply if we only use burst capacity intermittently (e.g., spikes twice a week)?

3) Cross-region bursting: we want a limited cross-region burst (max 10% of baseline) for DR. Is that technically feasible and how will it be billed?

4) SOC2 & audit artifacts: procurement asked for copies of attestations and a short checklist of logs and retention windows (they want to confirm audit coverage for six months post-integration).

Assume we'll likely move toward a balanced plan, but Procurement wants the answers above before we confirm. Can we get language by EOD Thursday?

— Liam
Liam Connor
Head of ML Platform | Orbitus Health

Liam — thanks, good questions. I’ve captured answers below and attached a short SOW excerpt you can drop into your procurement review. Highlights first, then the mechanics.

Answers (short):
- Baseline isolation / no-preempt language: yes — we will include the dedicated isolation clause for committed baseline GPUs (we will not schedule preemptible workloads on those devices). Wording included in attached SOW excerpt under Section 2.1.
- Warm standby credits: credits apply against measured standby time. Example: if you have a monthly baseline and the warm standby usage is averaging 40 hours/month, the 10% credit is applied against billed usage above baseline for that month (not against committed fees). If standby is used only sporadically (twice weekly spikes), credits pro-rate monthly and still apply to usage invoiced above baseline.
- Cross-region burst (DR): supported as a limited feature — we can allow up to 10% of baseline to burst to a secondary region during declared DR windows. Billing: cross-region burst is billed at the same usage rate as standard burst but includes a 5% regional-traffic surcharge to cover egress and warm provision costs. Please note SLAs for cross-region burst are best-effort and require a DR playbook signed by both parties.
- SOC2 & artifacts: attached SOC2-readme.txt (and we will provide the full SOC2 report via secure link under NDA). Artifact checklist included: control mappings, retention windows (token logs: 90 days; audit logs: 12 months by default; longer retention available as an add-on).

Detailed activation mechanics (excerpt):
- Tranche triggers: each activation tranche is gated by a go/no-go checklist (networking, IAM, smoke tests, baseline performance targets).
- Prewarm duration: recommended 72–120 hours per tranche to prepopulate KV and reduce tail-percentile latency.
- Automatic ramp guard: we include an autoscale guard that will not exceed your committed baseline unless explicitly authorized by your on-call or an agreed policy (we can include an authorization token flow for bursts).
- Decommit policy: earliest decommit permitted after month 12 of contract; decommit requires 60 days notice and will be applied at tranche boundaries.

Commercial clarifications:
- We have a two-tier pricing arrangement for Plan A (Balanced): baseline GPU-month fee + usage fee for burst. If you choose >=72 GPU baseline, we switch to the volume-discounted bracket which reduces baseline unit rate by 12%.
- Example cost snapshot (monthly): Plan A baseline (48 GPUs) estimated billed baseline = $XXX,XXX (see PDF for exact numbers tied to region and selected HW). Burst usage is variable.

Attached: updated Orbitus_Dedicated_Offer_v3.pdf (includes SOW excerpt and pricing table), activation_timetable.csv (detailed month-by-month ramp with triggers), SOC2-readme.txt.

If this addresses Procurement's asks, I propose we schedule a 30-minute alignment call on Monday to confirm Plan A and sign the SOW. DocuSign is ready pending the final SOW adjustments.

Best,
Irene
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
